SMTO-CFG-0007 — The Gateway couldn't start: its SMTO server port is invalid

GUID: f0047b55-9a73-4771-81c3-c1e40eab5d09
Slug: gateway-config-gateway-server-port-must-be-between-1
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer, stopped right after starting. The port number it was given for reaching your SMTO server isn't a real port number. No settings were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, find the server port in the command or settings used to start it: the --server-port option (ServerPort on Windows) or GATEWAY_SERVER_PORT. The Gateway reads its server port from one of these places, and that value is the one it refused.
  2. Set it to the port your SMTO server uses, usually the number after the colon in SMTO's web address (for example 8011). It must be between 1 and 65535. The Gateway connects to SMTO on this port, so a number outside that range can never work.
  3. Start the Gateway again. Then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway. This shows whether the Gateway now starts with the corrected value and SMTO can reach it.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway keeps running after it starts, and in Settings › Setup › Gateways it shows Connected.

If it still fails

  • Copy the error shown where the Gateway was started (or select Copy error details if SMTO shows it) and send it to the person who set up this Gateway. Don't keep restarting it with the same port; it will stop the same way each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway settings validation rejected server_port (GATEWAY_SERVER_PORT, or the --server-port / -ServerPort start option) because it is below 0 or above 65535, so the Gateway did not start.

What this means

  • Gateway settings validation finds server_port below zero or above 65535; zero is allowed only when no server_host requires a usable port. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway settings validation finds server_port below zero or above 65535; zero is allowed only when no server_host requires a usable port.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the port and whether outbound server_host is set; zero has meaning only for an unconfigured outbound address.

How to fix it

  • Set GATEWAY_SERVER_PORT (or --server-port / -ServerPort, which override it) to the SMTO Server's listening port, 1–65535; 0 is accepted only when GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST is empty (inbound mode). Restart the Gateway after the change.
  • Set a valid controller port, keeping zero only when no outbound controller host is configured.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The port is 1–65535 for a configured host, or zero with no outbound host.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
